title: My oldschool arcade drift game after after 455 Opus iterations...
author: mrjanosf
selftext:
For my first game, 13 years ago I did all graphics and coding by myself:  
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O5n9FhYm0Z8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O5n9FhYm0Z8)

For the second one, I hired a developer:  
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j5YGLEcwjeE](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j5YGLEcwjeE)

And here we are, now I'm just burning tokens...

comments.author: scottgwaters
comments.body:
Are you doIng any CPU drivers? Or is it all solo racing? I’m having trouble in my dirtbike game to have connective races from CPU riders. 

Either a race is super easy or impossible to beat other racers. I’ve gone through crazy tokens trying to solve this

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body: Almost every good racing game has to use some form of cheating or specialized mechanic in order to be fun in single player.

replies.author: scottgwaters
replies.body: Yeah, it’s been tricky. I need a Userbase of people who play the game before I can even developed the game. I have set my game up to just track every single race anonymously now. So once it is out there, it’ll get better and better more people play it hopefully.

replies.author: DudeWithASweater
replies.body:
Honestly, that's an issue even the biggest games suffer from.

Beginner mode on any racing game is basically just free first places for every single race.

I would try to tune it so that you're basing it off of real human players results. So that easy cpus are equal to a newbie racer who just picked up the game, harder cpus are more equal to someone like yourself who knows the mechanics and is much more capable.

replies.author: mrjanosf
replies.body: Yeah, that's how I would approach this...

replies.author: mrjanosf
replies.body: I'm planning to. I will update you here if I managed to figure it out.

replies.author: completelypositive
replies.body:
I'm a bit late but why don't you go and download roms of every racing game you can find, like 20 of them. Then grab reverse engineer anything, and have it figure out now all of those games did it, and see what it can create?

"I'm stuck with my race being too hard or too easy. Using tools, review these games and their code to understand how they did it, and then without copy and pasting their work, revise our code to better meet the feel I want" or whatever

replies.author: scottgwaters
replies.body: This is a great idea. There’s actually some deep dives on Mario kart 64 and a few other games where the source code has been figured out.

comments.author: Stunning-Relation564
comments.body: sick! how r u building it tho? unity, unreal, HTML, or what? also do u have playble link/download

replies.author: mrjanosf
replies.body:
No unity, no unreal, no html.  
  
C++20, bgfx (Metal / Vulkan / OpenGL / D3D)

replies.author: mrjanosf
replies.body: I'm gonna upload it to Steam as a free demo with drifting and time attack game modes and 2 maps.
